title: Tooling: 11.87x prepared geometry for complete exact bit-word checks
body:
Repeated checks of candidate words for the selected bit supplier recompute identical E8 geometry. This adds an opt-in, source-pinned prepared checker that reuses only validated non-gate state and runs every candidate through the original full symbolic replay, retained COPY totals and interface checks. Any non-gate JSON change uses the full checker. Frozen files and selected frontier are untouched.

**Status: tooling improvement; no new construction or kappa.** On Linux x86_64 / CPython 3.12.3, nine paired checks over three identical input words measured **11.87x median speedup** (1.44045s vs 0.12134s) and **5.12x batch speedup including 1.38884s preparation**. These measurements apply to that workload; timings never decide correctness.

Validation compares complete receipts or rejection type/message for 16 fixtures on all 661 symbolic columns, including dirty-target leakage, missing restoration, bad operands/frames, changed geometry/scatter, and a scalar-valid word with H4=false. Four controls cover template/returned-state isolation and checker pin invalidation. The committed semantic receipt is reproduced exactly. The API exposes its own loaded `Reject` class through `reject_type`.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-prepared-geometry-seed7
```

Expected: `PASS_BIT_PREPARED_GEOMETRY`, then `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. Add `--benchmark` to direct `verify.py` execution to reproduce timing. Registered replay, `make selected-record-check`, binding-only research baseline and `git diff --check` pass. A complete selected native cold replay was not run for this isolated opt-in tool.

OS assignment seed7, bit track; base `81e81af67714bdc8d1693b0bf5c29468b92f62ff`. Final upstream refresh `2de86c77b4127d2f01f504e0c7c5e4db737caa3c`; both live inputs are unchanged. Exact blobs/SHA256 and scope argument are in the package. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1653.

One evidence-driven pivot: the initial single-A-write/no-A-donor helper screen found zero eligible helpers; this is a tooling side result and does not satisfy the bit-helper-contract construction acceptance gate or settle the broader carried-basis mechanism. Scope and open next question are explicit in TASK.json/README.

Credit: eumemic's PR555 frozen checker and DreamingOfClouds' PR589 tuned word. Concurrent thakrarsagar PR1584 optimizes finite-bit block-core transitions, a distinct workload and not a dependency. Cinna Davis (1337isnot1337), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.
